confirm.text: One form today carries a selection from the "What did we observe?" list that needs the technician's confirmation. Per Kelby Hammer, technicians may select "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose, so these are reported as items to confirm, not as confirmed events.

Brianda Sandoval — XTO, Germania Spraberry Unit 4507H, job 36735, 11/08 04:22 PM. All ten items in the list were selected, including "Unsafe conditions" and "Stop work authority was discussed". Note the selected item is the discussed variant, which is a routine pre-job item — "Stop work authority utilized" was not selected, so no stop-work event is indicated.

This one is not the blind mis-selection pattern. The form carries a narrative that names an actual condition: "crew had to disconnect flowlines on wellhead. slippery/muddy conditions", with "What Went Well? Continued" reading "crew managed to complete the job despite the rain and mud." The Learn section was completed ("communication regarding weather"). The selection appears to be a real observation of wet-weather conditions, not a carried-forward click. Worth confirming with her what, if anything, needed intervention.

Separately, selecting all ten items at once is itself the carry-forward pattern worth watching, so it is possible the narrative is genuine while some of the ten selections were not individually considered.
No technician on today's list has appeared on this list in the recent reviews on record.

Trailer forms of both kinds, and the equipment sections of the H2S daily, are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates, SCBA and workpack inspection sheet entries, and 4-gas calibration dates all exist only inside the images, not as extractable text — so this review can confirm that a photograph was taken and when, but not what it shows.

Two further limits apply to today specifically. This review runs at 11:00 PM Central, so any form submitted in the final hour of the day is not captured here. And because the review ran before the following morning, the usual second sweep for late-arriving submissions could not be performed — a form for 11/08 that lands overnight or tomorrow morning would not appear above. Both would show up in tomorrow's review.

19 of 19 submissions read. The job board was available: the 11/8/2026 boards from Blake Walton were used, both the ArkLaTex and Permian Basin workbooks, sheet "11-8" on each. 20 manned board rows were checked for coverage — 9 on the ArkLaTex board and 11 on the Permian board, excluding rows marked CANCELLED, ON STANDBY, DAYS OFF, WTX SUPPORT and CONTINGENCY / SHOP.
